correctness.rationale: Every resident constraint is exactly one interval on a sum of at most two binary sites; componentwise two-state DP reconstructs min and max. For two feasible assignments the only forbidden mixed pair states are encoded by implications between opposite-sign disagreements. Their strongly connected components occupy alternating paths or even cycles and have occupancy change at most one. Reverse topological switching preserves feasibility and crosses every intermediate cardinality. A seven-vertex degree-three star-subdivision has precisely feasible sizes {1,3}. Brute-force comparison and 10000-site construction passed, but are not substitutes for the proof.

originality.rationale: The original arbitrary-interval degree-two result uses a cardinality-indexed dynamic program rather than a no-gap structural theorem or linear-time any-size witness, while the later linear-time result is restricted to lower bound zero. The proof here establishes a new implication-SCC interpolation for arbitrary positive/zero lower and upper approvals, with a seven-vertex sharp boundary. Semantically similar results in general binary-CSP literature remain a priority risk.

value.rationale: The exact feasible-intake spectrum is a natural resource-planning invariant. Positive lower quotas destroy the trivial downward-closed property of the previous upper-bound-only model. Proving no gaps and constructing any specified feasible intake in linear time on all degree-two networks is a structural strengthening with a sharp degree-three boundary.
